Windows only lets programs read the CPU': Windows only lets programs read the CPU's, motherboard's, memory's and drives' sensors through a hardware driver. LibreHardwareMonitor is a free, open-source monitor with that driver; while it runs, Daisy's App reads its numbers and adds:
• CPU temperature and power on the Temps: • CPU temperature and power on the Temps tile, and in the log
• Motherboard, memory, drive and GPU hot: • Motherboard, memory, drive and GPU hot-spot temperatures
• Fan speeds, voltages, power, clocks an: • Fan speeds, voltages, power, clocks and more in a Hardware sensors section
Download LibreHardwareMonitor (the .zip: Download LibreHardwareMonitor (the .zip from the latest release).
Unzip it to a folder it can stay in, and: Unzip it to a folder it can stay in, and run LibreHardwareMonitor.exe. Windows asks for administrator approval: it needs that to read the sensors.
. It uses port 8085; if you change it, s: . It uses port 8085; if you change it, set the same address in Settings → Hardware → Performance.

The CPU temperature and power also appear on the Temps tile in Hardware → Performance.
